architectural_notes: Infra: the reverse path of the Alembic revision, verified by running up then down on the paired branch. The down migration re-adds the inventory_code column and reconstructs each value from the canonical location plus split-out batch and serial, restoring the combined column. This is the core of PI1-migration-reversible and NFR-F6-reversibility; reconstruction is owned by the migration script (with the join rule mirroring the service parse rule) and confirmed via app/repositories against the branch, not a mock.
given: a stock record that has been migrated up to first-class batch_number and serial_number columns with the combined column dropped
then: a combined inventory_code is reconstructed from the canonical location plus the split-out batch and serial, and the combined column is restored

independence.rationale: Prior ACs cover the forward migration and reporting; AC6 covers the reverse path. The up migration could be entirely correct while the down path is missing or reconstructs the code wrongly, so reversibility breaks independently.
